tools.name: hello
tools.description: Returns a greeting with the signature and trace lines. Used to check that the server answers.

tools.name: pick_tool
tools.description: Lists the Act 60 tools as cards grouped by lifecycle stage, best matches for the request first. Call it when a request matches several tools or none.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Reports the state of a multi-day job (for example a donation campaign) by the job id its tool returned.

tools.name: next_deadlines
tools.description: Lists the next Act 60 compliance dates for a segment and regime (annual report, CPA report, CECFL list year, federal return, Form 8898, Chapter 3 filings), each with the canon passage that sets it, its verified-on date and regime tag. Dates no verified source states are left out.

tools.name: calendar_feed
tools.description: Returns an ICS calendar feed URL with the Act 60 compliance dates for a segment and regime, each event citing its rule. No login and no contact; the URL holds only the segment, regime, decree year and language.

tools.name: remind_me
tools.description: Schedules reminders 30, 7 and 1 days before chosen Act 60 deadlines, each citing its rule, on the verified contact of this session only: it never subscribes another address. A guest is asked for a verified contact first. It stores the reminders, the channel and language preference and a subscription

tools.name: delete_my_data
tools.description: Deletes the data of the person behind this session and never anyone else’s: with account true, the account this conversation is linked to (every contact and job merged into it); with contact, the verified contact of this session, which must match. tools.name: whats_changed
tools.description: Lists the approved change notes on the Act 60 primary sources (Act 60-2019 as amended, Act 38-2026, DDEC, Hacienda, CECFL, IRS) dated on or after `since`, newest first, each with English and Spanish summaries and the source URL. Only notes a person approved are listed; an empty list means no approve

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: whats_changed · Private data: calendar_feed, remind_me, delete_my_data · Public sink: delete_my_data · Destructive: delete_my_data.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: whats_changed · Private data: calendar_feed, remind_me, delete_my_data · Public sink: delete_my_data · Destructive: delete_my_data

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
